# Discovery reference

The worked example, pre-meeting brief, recap, question bank and customer call script for
[the Discovery section](SKILL.md#discovery). Open it only when you need it.

## Worked example

### Problem card

```markdown
### Weekly invoice reconciliation takes too long
- Job: Reconcile supplier invoices before payment
- Workaround: Export two spreadsheets and compare them by hand
- Cost: About 20 staff-hours a month: two people, 10 hours each
- Who feels it: Finance operations
- How often: Every Friday
- Evidence: Walkthrough of the latest reconciliation and its two spreadsheets
```

The brief's Summary names the card as "Weekly invoice reconciliation takes too long", and so does
the spec's Why, with what the workaround costs.

### Options and payback

Offer two to four options, the recommendation first. Each option that builds something gets its
own payback line, from rounded rates (500 a day, 50 an hour), never real salaries.

- **Recommended: Smallest slice.** Flag the rows whose invoice totals differ. The walkthrough
  showed finding mismatches is the slow part, and it pays back in 2.0 months.
- **Match and post every invoice.** Pays back in 12.5 months, so don't build it yet.
- **Don't build.** The team keeps comparing by hand, at about 20 staff-hours a month.

```text
forge spec payback --build-days 2 --day-rate 500 --hours-per-month 10 --people 2 --hourly-rate 50 --confidence estimated
build: 2.0 months
```

```text
forge spec payback --build-days 15 --day-rate 500 --hours-per-month 12 --people 2 --hourly-rate 50 --confidence estimated
don't build: 12.5 months
```

Recommend the option with the fewest months among those answering "build" or "smallest slice
first"; a tie goes to the smaller build. If none does, recommend "don't build", or "find out
first" when an option's value can't be estimated yet:

```text
forge spec payback --build-days 2 --day-rate 500
find out first
```

When the hours come from a card field that still reads `unknown`, the numbers are a guess, so
leave `--confidence` at its default, guessed:

```text
forge spec payback --build-days 2 --day-rate 500 --hours-per-month 10 --people 2 --hourly-rate 50
smallest slice first: 5.0 months
```

The human's choice and one line of why go into the spec's `## Behaviour`:

```markdown
Chosen: Smallest slice, flag mismatched rows. It pays back in about two months, and mismatches
are where the time goes.
```

### Success measure

```markdown
## Success measure
- Metric: Staff-hours spent reconciling invoices each month
- Baseline: 20 hours
- Target: 5 hours or less
- Check date: 2026-12-31
```

Once every story from the spec is done and the date has passed, `forge next` lists the check, and
`forge spec measure <slug> --result "<measured result>"` records it in a fix.

## Pre-meeting brief

One page in `docs/context/`, drafted from the prospect's website before the first meeting.

```markdown
# <Prospect>: pre-meeting brief
- Likely jobs: <what their people do each week>
- Their terms: <words the site uses for their work>

### <short problem title> (guess)
- Job: <guess>
- Workaround: <guess>
- Cost: unknown

## First five questions
1. <about the last time a guessed problem happened>
```

## Recap

Drafted in `docs/context/` the same day as the meeting, for the customer to confirm.

```markdown
# <Prospect>: recap of <YYYY-MM-DD>
- Your problem: <in their words>
- What it costs: <in their numbers>
- The demo will cover: <the one task, start to finish>
- Who signs off: <name and role>
- Still to find out: <each open "ask the client" question>
- Demo date: <YYYY-MM-DD>
```

Their reply is the source of the Demo workflow and Sign-off person answers:
`- Demo workflow: <task> (client, <YYYY-MM-DD>)` and
`- Sign-off person: <name, role> (client, <YYYY-MM-DD>)`.

## Question bank

Ask one question per turn, about a past event, choosing the one that fills a missing card field.

- Job: "Tell me about the last time you reconciled supplier invoices."
- Workaround: "What did you do after you found the totals didn't match?"
- Cost: "How long did the last reconciliation take?"
- Who feels it: "Who else had to help with that reconciliation?"
- How often: "When did it happen before that?"
- Evidence: "Could you show me the spreadsheet or report you used that time?"

Until the engineer says they know why you ask, add one short `Why I ask:` line to each question.
Ask what happened before asking what the customer wants built.

## Customer call script

1. Set the frame: "I want to understand how this works today. I'm not here to pitch a solution."
2. Ask one question about the last time the problem happened, with its `Why I ask:` line.
3. Follow that event through the workaround, cost, people, frequency and evidence, one question
   per turn, skipping fields already answered.
4. Ask for the spreadsheet or form they use today; keep only its column headers, never its rows.
   Write each word they use for their work under `## Words they use`.
5. Read the card back in the customer's words, ask for corrections, and write what is still
   missing as `unknown`.
6. End discovery before talking about solutions. Then offer neutral choices for facts, or a
   separate decision with the recommendation first.

## Constitution defaults

- How do people sign in?: Email and password. Social sign-in comes with the story that needs it.
- Can people see each other's information, or only their own?: Each person sees only their organisation's information; roles are admin and member. Built in when the app has libs/organisations or apps/api/app/organisations.
- Who can add people and change what they can do?: Admins invite people by email. Built in when the app has libs/organisations or apps/api/app/organisations.
- How many people will use it, and how many at the same time?: Up to 100 users, with 10 at once, on managed hosting with managed Postgres.
- How much information will it hold in a year (rows, files)?: Postgres and server-side pages. File storage comes with the story that adds uploads.
- Does anything you enter today live in a spreadsheet or old system? Should we bring it in?: No import; add CSV import later if needed.
- Should it work with no internet (for example in the field)?: Online only, with a clear offline message.
- What devices: phones, tablets, desktop? Which matters most?: Desktop first, fully responsive down to phone.
- Do people need to pay in the app (one time, subscription, invoices)?: No payments; choose a provider in a later story if payments are needed.
- Should the app send messages (email, text, push, in-app)? About what?: Transactional email. In-app notices come with the story that needs them. No text or push messages.
- Which languages and currencies, date formats, time zones?: English. A message catalogue comes with the story that adds a second language. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD and times use 24-hour format in the user's time zone. Currency uses INR with the currency code (INR 1,234.56). Numbers use comma thousands separators and a decimal point (1,234.56). The date, time, number and money formats are built in when the app has libs/organisations or apps/api/app/organisations.
- Does it need to connect to other tools (calendar, accounting, CRM, maps, email)?: None by default; add integrations as later stories.
- What happens if someone deletes something by mistake? Do you need history of who changed what?: Soft delete with a confirm step; keep change history for admin actions. Built in when the app has libs/organisations or apps/api/app/organisations.
- Do you need reports, charts or exports (PDF, Excel)?: CSV export from each table and a summary dashboard. The CSV export is built in when the app has libs/organisations or apps/api/app/organisations.
- Should the public see any part of it (a landing page, a public form)?: Keep everything behind sign-in; add a simple public page later if needed.
- Do you have a logo, colours or a style you must match?: shadcn neutral theme, light and dark.
- Do you need to upload files or images? How large?: No uploads; if a story needs them, set a 10 MB limit and use S3-compatible storage.
- Who fixes problems, and how fast must it be back up if it breaks?: Daily managed backups and no uptime promise. Each error is logged with its error id, and Mainline alerts on the error log lines; the app has no error-tracking service.
- Is there a date you must launch by, and a budget for running costs per month?: Low-cost managed services.
- Does anyone need to use it with a screen reader or have other access needs?: WCAG 2.2 AA.
- Show me an app you like. What do you like about it?: shadcn dashboard-01 style.

## Bad-to-better questions

| Avoid | Ask instead |
|---|---|
| "Would you use an app that fixes this?" | "What did you do the last time this happened?" |
| "How often does this happen?" | "When was the previous time it happened?" |
| "Would automation save you time?" | "How long did the last manual reconciliation take?" |
| "What features do you want?" | "What happened after you found a mismatch?" |
| "Is this a big problem?" | "What work was delayed the last time this happened?" |
